CR-JOBS-07#/statement.basis: Synchronous owned-value service boundaries commit both receipt transactions before remote suspension. All43 additional/native/desktop inventory hits are bound to reviewed code: productive Store access is in closed synchronous byte/project captures or Arc identity comparison; custody reservations retain handles rather than database/transaction guards; other hits are declarations/test fixtures.

CR-PROJECT-04#/statement.basis: Motionwright owns StudioService and its Arc<Mutex<Store>>, Store owns its rusqlite Connection and application Project values. Native Application receives an observer and handlers that use that same service; desktop startup opens its application SQLite path. The additional Graph boundary calls the same Store.apply. No Native SDK reference store becomes the authority. No simultaneous-client runtime acceptance is inferred.

CR-SDK-02#/statement.basis: Ordinary Native handlers delegate to StudioService.apply with the Host-derived project stamp and original request ID; StudioService delegates to application Store.apply. The dedicated Graph handler obtains its Host permit first and then calls the trusted service admission seam, which preserves that request and uses the same Store transaction. This is the actual source delegation path, not proof of Host authorization behavior or UI/native concurrency.

CR-SDK-05#/acceptance_criterion.basis: The exact D4 oracle binds all80 OperationKind variants and registrations to the one explicit descriptor constructor; mounted and denied Graph variants use graph_contract through the same constructor, giving81 registered operation names. Mutating risk, Idempotent,15000ms timeout,dry_run=false,DurableRequestKey,undo=None and ApplicationTransaction are explicit. No mutation is declared MutatingReversible or given an application undo guarantee by the constructor. Both document and Graph handlers pass the actual context request_id through service into Store.apply. Source shows payload-bound duplicate-key lookup before mutation and committed result receipts; this is source evidence of same-request replay, not a replay execution. SDK pin01d cooperation.rs defines separate StateIdempotent and DurableRequestKey retry semantics. Its OperationContract.validate rejects Idempotent only when retry is Never; DurableRequestKey is a permitted explicit replay guarantee. This resolves the question whether the common Idempotent declaration necessarily promises state-idempotence under different keys. The Native SDK explicitly rejects advertised dry_run support in its cooperation layer. Motionwright declares false; this is faithful absence disclosure rather than a positive dry-run capability. External renderer/Host commands are outside this app document registry; their own guarantees are not inferred from these descriptors.
